scenes.headline: The Path of Selfless Service
visual: Karma-yoga: work as an offering
scenes.say: Chapter Three. The Path of Selfless Service, Karma-yoga. Krishna has praised knowledge and a calm mind. Now Arjuna asks the obvious question.

scenes.headline: Then why must I fight?
visual: If knowledge is better than action…
…why push me into this terrible deed?
Your words confuse me. Tell me one thing
scenes.say: If you think knowledge is better than action, Arjuna says, then why do you urge me into this terrible war? Your words seem mixed, and they confuse my mind. Tell me, decisively, the one thing by which I may reach the highest good. It is a fair question, and the whole chapter answers it.
Krishna begins by saying there are two paths, not one. Verse three. {verse}

scenes.headline: No one can stop acting
visual: Not starting work does not free you
Even keeping the body alive is action
Restraining the body while the mind roams is hypocrisy
scenes.say: But no one, Krishna says, can live without acting, even for a moment. Nature drives every creature to act. Simply refusing to work does not set anyone free, and even keeping the body alive requires action. Worse is the person who holds the body still while the mind dwells on pleasures. Krishna calls that person a hypocrite.
So the answer is not to stop working, but to change why we work. Verse nine. {verse}

scenes.headline: The wheel of creation
visual: The creator made humans together with service
Serve, and be served in return
The one who only takes lives in vain
scenes.say: Then Krishna tells a story of creation. In the beginning, the creator made human beings together with selfless service and said: by this you will prosper. Serve the powers of nature, and they will nourish you. By caring for one another you will reach the highest good. Whoever only takes from this great cycle, giving nothing back, lives in vain.
And leaders carry a special duty, because others copy them. Verse twenty. {verse}
Then Krishna points to himself. Verse twenty-two. {verse} If he ever stopped, he says, people everywhere would follow his example, and the world would fall into confusion.
Who is actually doing all this work? Verse twenty-seven. {verse}
Arjuna then asks: what drives a person to do wrong, even against their own will, as if pushed by force? Krishna answers in one word. Verse thirty-seven. {verse}
He paints it in three pictures. Verse thirty-eight. {verse}

visual: No one can be idle, even for a moment
Nature drives every being to act
Stopping work does not bring freedom
scenes.say: Lesson one. Action is unavoidable; no one can be truly idle. Every living being is driven to act by the forces of nature. So the question is never whether you will act. The question is how, and why.

visual: Human life was designed around service
Working for others aligns you with nature
Selfish work pulls against it
scenes.say: Lesson two. Selfless service, seva, is the foundation of a well-ordered life. The creator built service into human life from the start. When you work for the good of others, not only for yourself, you move with the grain of the universe instead of against it.

visual: Duty without attachment becomes worship
Offer the work to God or the greater good
No task is just a task
scenes.say: Lesson three. All work done as duty is a form of worship. A duty done without clinging to its fruits, and offered to God or to the greater good, becomes an act of devotion. Washing dishes, writing code, caring for a parent: you are never just doing a task.

scenes.headline: Why the work is done
visual: For personal reward | For universal welfare
Creates karmic bondage | Liberates
Anxious about the outcome | Calm in any outcome
Serves the ego | Serves the world
scenes.say: Lesson four. Perform your duty for universal welfare, not personal reward. Work done only for your own benefit binds you. The same work done as service, for the good of all and without attachment to outcomes, sets you free. That is the essence of Karma-yoga.

visual: Whatever the great do, others follow
Leaders set the standard
Even God acts to set an example
scenes.say: Lesson five. Leaders and wise people must set the example. Whatever noble people do, others copy, and whatever standard they set, the world follows. Krishna himself keeps acting, though he has nothing to gain, simply to keep the world on its path.

visual: The three gunas of nature do all the work
The ego claims to be the doer
Wrongly claimed doership creates karma
scenes.say: Lesson six. Nature does all the work; the ego falsely claims it. Every action is carried out by the three forces of nature. The ego, the sense of being a separate doer, takes the credit and the blame, and that false claim is what binds us.

visual: Don't shake the faith of those still learning
Inspire by doing your own work well
Example teaches more than argument
scenes.say: Lesson seven. Do not unsettle the minds of the spiritually immature. People who are still attached to the fruits of their work should not be confused or mocked by the wise. Inspire them instead, by doing your own work well and without attachment. Example teaches more than argument.

visual: Do every duty with a spiritual frame of mind
Free from desire, attachment and grief
Dedicate each action to the Divine
scenes.say: Lesson eight. Dedicate all your actions to God, or to truth. Krishna asks Arjuna to fight with his mind fixed on the Divine, free from desire, attachment and grief. That inner dedication changes the meaning of every act, even the hardest one.

visual: Even the wise act according to their nature
Forcing an unnatural path brings strain
Your own dharma, done imperfectly, is better
scenes.say: Lesson nine. Everyone acts according to their own nature. Even the wisest person follows their deep nature, their svabhava. Forcing yourself into a path that is completely unnatural to you brings strain and failure. Krishna says it is better to do your own duty imperfectly than another's perfectly.

visual: Likes and dislikes live in the senses
Do not come under their control
They are the two great stumbling blocks
scenes.say: Lesson ten. Likes and dislikes are the two great stumbling blocks. Attraction and aversion are natural to the senses. The danger is letting them decide for you. Notice them, but do not hand them the wheel.

visual: Lust is intense desire for pleasure
Unfulfilled, it becomes anger
It clouds wisdom like smoke covers fire
scenes.say: Lesson eleven. Lust, intense desire, is the root enemy of wisdom. When desire is frustrated, it turns into anger, and when it persists, it clouds judgment the way smoke covers a fire or dust covers a mirror. Krishna calls it the enemy within.

scenes.headline: The ladder within
visual: Body
Senses
Mind
Intellect
Spirit
scenes.say: Lesson twelve. The path to overcoming lust is to master the ladder of the self. The senses are higher than the body. The mind is higher than the senses. The intellect is higher than the mind. And the Spirit is higher still. Know the Spirit, steady the mind with the intellect, and you can defeat this mighty enemy.

visual: Self-knowledge, for the contemplative
Selfless action, for everyone else
Both lead to the same goal
scenes.say: Lesson thirteen. Two paths exist: self-knowledge and selfless action. The spiritual path is not one size fits all. The contemplative may walk the path of knowledge. Most of us, living active lives, walk the path of selfless work. Both arrive at the same place.

visual: Holding the body still while the mind indulges
Krishna calls this hypocrisy
Real discipline is inner
scenes.say: Lesson fourteen. Hypocrisy is worse than honest action. Someone who outwardly renounces pleasures but inwardly dwells on them is deceiving themselves. Better to act honestly in the world with a disciplined mind than to pretend to renounce it.

scenes.headline: The wheel of creation
visual: Selfless service
God is pleased
Nature provides
Life is sustained
Service again
scenes.say: Lesson fifteen. The wheel of creation must be kept in motion. Selfless service pleases God, the powers of nature respond and provide, food sustains every body, and that life is offered back in service. There is a sacred interdependence here, and whoever refuses to play their part lives in vain.

scenes.headline: Keep working, but change why
visual: No one can stop acting
Act as service, offered to the Divine
Master the senses, and defeat desire
scenes.say: So, Chapter Three. No one can stop acting, so don't try. Change why you act instead: work as service, offered to something greater than yourself. Keep the wheel turning, set a good example, and master the senses, so that desire cannot steal your wisdom. Next, Krishna reveals how ancient this teaching really is.
